newsitem.title: USA: MSRB offers raft of new rules on bond underwriting.
newsitem.headline: MSRB offers raft of new rules on bond underwriting.

text.p: MSRB's chairman on Tuesday called on all corners of the muni bond market for comment on an array of draft rules aimed at raising public confidence in the bond underwriting process.

"All of us -- underwriters, issuers, counsel, and financial advisers -- have a responsibility to see that the underwriting of a new issue is efficient and above reproach, Roger Hayes, managing director of NationsBanc Capital Markets, Inc., said in a written statement.

The 22-page rule package, which was approved by the 15-member Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board at its quarterly meeting April 30 and May 1, proposes new disclosure standards for bond syndicates, financial advisers and underwriters.

It will appear on the board's website this week and in its quarterly filing to dealers, MSRB Reports, in two weeks. If MSRB adopts the rules, they go to the Securities and Exchange Commission for review. SEC will publish them for public comment and then vote whether to make them final.
The MSRB's draft rules for syndicates would do the following:

* Require managing underwriters to keep a record of all syndicate rules set by issuers, including rules on syndicate formation, order review, designation policies and bond allocations. If an issuer does not publish its guidelines, the underwriter would keep on file its own detailed summary of the issuer's informal guidelines.
* Require managing underwriters to give syndicate members a copy of guidelines before the team's first offer of bonds.
Syndicate members would furnish the summary "promptly" to others, on request. The issuer of the deal would get a copy.

* Require senior syndicate managers to allocate bonds within 24 hours of sending the commitment wire; disclose designations to syndicate members within five business days after sale date; disclose to syndicate members - by final settlement of the syndicate account - a summary of all bonds allocated to each member, by maturity; disclose to syndicate members, in writing, within 10 business days of the sale date, the amount of any portion of the take-down that is directed to each member of the syndicate by the issuer.
* Move the deadline for payment of designations from 30 business days after delivery of bonds to the customer, to 30 calendar days after the issuer delivers the securities to the syndicate.

* Move final settlement of syndicate accounts from 60 calendar days after all securities have been delivered to syndicate members to 30 calendar days after the issuer delivers securities to the syndicate.
The MSRB's draft disclosure rules for financial advisers and underwriters would:

* Require dealers acting advisers to state in writing whether they received or have "an understanding to receive" payments from anyone regarding an offering, including source, basis and estimated amount. That includes advisers acting as issuers' agents, such as on swap deals. A similar rule would apply to underwriters of negotiated deals. Underwriters also would have to tell issuers in writing whether they have or plan to make any payments regarding the issue.

* Require an adviser to state in writing whether it is acting as principal in a transaction associated with advisory services. Exempt from disclosure any payments to an adviser acting as a principal in a transaction with the issuer associated with its services.
* Require the adviser to document services it will provide an issuer and the "basis of compensation." Adviser also would notify issuer promptly in writing of any changes in that plan.

* Require a dealer acting as both adviser and remarketing agent for an issue "to meet the same disclosure requirements as a dealer acting as financial adviser and later negotiating the underwriting or acting as placement agent for the issue."
*Exempt from disclosure any payments made to or received by syndicate members from the underwriting spread.
Regarding primary market disclosure, MSRB asked whether it should require disclosure to investors whenever an issuer is involved in selecting underwriters' counsel.
